13 A mass of 500 g is attached at one end of a rod of length 1.50 m. The rod is pivoted at a distance
of 25 cm from the other end. The rod is horizontal.
pivot
rod
mass 500 g
25 cm
1.50 m
What is the moment about the pivot due to the mass?
A
0.63 N m
B
1.2 N m
C
6.1 N m
D
7.4 N m

hints: Look at the diagram distances: the $500 \text{ g}$ mass is $1.50 \text{ m}$ from the left end but the pivot is $25 \text{ cm}$ from that end, so find the pivot-to-mass distance first.
Recall that the moment is $force \times perpendicular distance$ and the force here is the weight of the mass, $W = mg$, not $500 \text{ g}$ itself.
Convert $500 \text{ g}$ to $0.50 \text{ kg}$ and $25 \text{ cm}$ to $0.25 \text{ m}$, then calculate $mg$ times $(1.50 - 0.25) \text{ m}$ to compare with the $\text{N m}$ options.
walkthrough: Identify the force: the mass pulls down with its weight $W = mg$. Convert $500 \text{ g} = 0.50 \text{ kg}$, so $W = 0.50 \times 9.81 = 4.905 \text{ N}$.
Identify the perpendicular distance from the line of the weight to the pivot. The rod is horizontal so the weight acts vertically at $90$ degrees to the rod.
From the diagram, mass to left end is $1.50 \text{ m}$ and pivot to left end is $25 \text{ cm} = 0.25 \text{ m}$, so pivot to mass is $d = 1.50 - 0.25 = 1.25 \text{ m}$.
Calculate $4.905 \times 1.25 = 6.13 \text{ N m}$, which to two significant figures is $6.1 \text{ N m}$ with unit $\text{N m}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This multiplies the mass in $\text{kg}$ by the distance, giving $0.50 \times 1.25 = 0.63$, but the moment needs weight $mg$ in $\text{N}$, not mass.

B.explanation: This uses the $25 \text{ cm}$ distance from the pivot to the left end, giving $4.9 \times 0.25$, instead of the distance from the pivot to the $500 \text{ g}$ mass.

C.explanation: Weight $mg$ multiplied by the correct $1.25 \text{ m}$ perpendicular distance gives about $6.1 \text{ N m}$ clockwise about the pivot.

D.explanation: This uses the full rod length $1.50 \text{ m}$ as the distance, giving $4.9 \times 1.50$, and forgets to subtract the $25 \text{ cm}$ overhang.
